title: Testing Fundamentals and Test Case Design
learningObjectives: Explain test cases, arrange-act-assert, edge cases, deterministic tests and regression tests.
Select a suitable debugging or testing technique for PY21.7.
Interpret diagnostic information and test results correctly.
Identify limitations and risks when applying PY21.7.
Apply PY21.7 concepts in a maintainable Python workflow.

understand.concept: A test checks whether a unit of software behaves as expected for a defined input. Good tests are repeatable, focused and independent of accidental external state. A common structure is Arrange, Act, Assert: prepare inputs, call the behaviour and compare the result with the expected outcome. Test normal cases, boundaries and invalid inputs according to the function's contract.
understand.whyItMatters: Tests provide executable evidence that code meets its requirements and help detect regressions after changes.
understand.analogy: A test case is a controlled experiment: set up known conditions, perform one action and compare the result with a prediction.
understand.analogyLimit: Passing tests only provide evidence for the cases exercised; they cannot prove every possible execution is correct.
understand.summary: Testing Fundamentals and Test Case Design develops reliable debugging and software verification skills.

explain.narrative:
## Design useful test cases
Start with the behaviour contract: accepted inputs, expected outputs and documented errors. Keep each test focused on one behaviour. Prefer deterministic tests that do not depend on network access, wall-clock timing or shared mutable state. Use descriptive names that explain the scenario and expected outcome.

Include typical values, empty inputs, boundary values and invalid inputs. A regression test should capture a previously observed failure. Avoid tests that simply repeat implementation details without checking externally meaningful behaviour.

examples.title: Arrange, act and assert
examples.code:
values = [2, 3, 4]
result = sum(values)
expected = 9
print(result == expected)
examples.explanation: The example prepares data, performs an operation and checks the expected result.

examples.title: Test a boundary value
examples.explanation: A boundary test checks behaviour exactly at a limit.

examples.title: Test an empty collection
examples.explanation: Empty inputs are common edge cases for collection functions.

examples.title: Use descriptive case names
examples.explanation: Descriptive names communicate the scenario and expected outcome.

examples.title: Check several deterministic cases
examples.code:
def square(value):
    return value * value
cases = [(0, 0), (2, 4), (-3, 9)]
print(all(square(x) == expected for x, expected in cases))
examples.explanation: A small table of fixed inputs makes a deterministic regression check.

practise.guidedTask: Design a test table for a function that calculates a discount. Include ordinary, boundary, empty or invalid cases and explain the expected result for each.
practise.independentTask: Create a test plan for a list-processing function using Arrange-Act-Assert and at least one regression case.
